articles.title: Ahead of Reliance Industries investing in Texas refinery, Rubio to meet Ambani in Jamnagar
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: US secretary of state Marco Rubio will arrive in Mumbai Tuesday for a two-day visit to India that will see him travelling to Jamnagar as well.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: US secretary of state Marco Rubio will arrive in Mumbai Tuesday for a two-day visit to India that will see him travelling to Jamnagar as well. While his bilateral with counterpart S Jaishankar is scheduled for Tuesday in Mumbai, he will travel to Jamnagar the next day.The trip to Gujarat’s refinery hub, where he will visit the Reliance oil refining complex, is expected to last around nine hours. Rubio will also have a meeting with Mukesh Ambani before returning to Mumbai.The visit highlights growing India-US energy cooperation. Rubio is expected to focus on strategic energy partnerships, highlighting the importance of the Reliance oil refinery as the company prepares for its upcoming investment in a Texas oil refinery. Officials did not confirm or deny reports that Rubio may also visit the Vantara animal rehabilitation centre, located in the same complex.On his arrival in Mumbai, Rubio will briefly meet Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis and lay a wreath at the Taj Hotel memorial before joining Jaishankar for the bilateral meeting.This will be Rubio’s second bilateral meeting with Jaishankar in India this year, following his visit in May. They will meet again later this month on the margins of the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in Atlanta. Jaishankar is expected to prioritise India’s concerns related to immigration-related issues, while reviewing bilateral cooperation, reaffirming commitment to the trade deal under discussion and reiterating India’s position on energy security.Later in the evening, Jaishankar will join Rubio for the Freedom 250 reception to celebrate the US’s 250th anniversary at Jio Convention Centre. The ministry of external affairs has said Jaishankar will be the guest of honour. Although an official confirmation is still awaited, Rubio is also likely to meet Gautam Adani and Tata group chief N Chandrasekaran before his departure for Jamnagar Wednesday.You use AI every day. articles.title: Tata Trusts to build institutions, not just fund them: Noel
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Tata Trusts will put more weight on building institutions directly rather than only funding them, chairman Noel Tata said, as the charitable
articles.body: MUMBAI: Tata Trusts will put more weight on building institutions directly rather than only funding them, chairman Noel Tata said, as the charitable body’s differences with the Tata Sons board persist.In the Trusts’ FY26 annual report, Noel said the need was “not simply to support an existing effort, but to build institutions and models that can become enduring public assets in their own right”. He did not directly refer to the governance and strategic differences between the Trusts and Tata Sons.The Trusts, which draw dividends from Tata Sons, disbursed Rs 1,556 crore in FY26. Institutional grants took Rs 1,353 crore. Individuals received Rs 203 crore. The Trusts have long worked mainly through grants and funding support.Noel cast the shift as a return to the founders’ purpose. “Our founders did not set out to build the largest group of companies,” he wrote. “They believed that enterprise carried with it a responsibility to society, and that the true measure of progress was an improvement in the quality of people’s lives.”Its earlier institutions include Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru and Mumbai’s Tata Hospital.Noel named education as a priority. India needed more institutions that nurture talent at home, he said, so students are not forced to look overseas. In healthcare, the Trusts are working towards a network of 40-50 not-for-profit general hospitals.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: India on track for historic growth streakas global bodies raise forecasts above 7%
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Going by projections by global agencies, India is on course to surpass its 2003-2007 record of five consecutive years of 7% or higher growth,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Going by projections by global agencies, India is on course to surpass its 2003-2007 record of five consecutive years of 7% or higher growth, Kyunghoon Kim of Korea Institute for International Economic Policy said.Starting 2021, India has recorded a five-year average annual growth rate of 7.83%, marking the second-highest five-year average since 1960, Kim said in a social media post. Between 2003 and 2007, the economy had expanded at an average pace of 7.89%. “Sustaining such momentum over several years deserves attention,” Kim said.Following a 5.8% contraction during the pandemic, India’s economy rebounded sharply by 9.7% in 2021 and has sustained growth exceeding 7% in each subsequent year.After a 7.8% growth in the June quarter, most global outfits — from IMF and World Bank to OECD and rating agencies — have revised their projections to around 7% growth this year, making India the fastest growth major economy once again.Kim highlighted that the latest round of growth is on an expanded base as India’s GDP stood at over $1 trillion in 2007 and is now approaching $4 trillion. A 7% expansion now delivers larger absolute additions to national output. “It is projected to become the world’s third-largest economy around 2030,” he said.While structural and global headwinds remain, he noted that maintaining such sustained high-velocity growth across a population of 1.4 billion represents a milestone achievement. “I hope economists at major institutions and I will once again be adding a few decimal points to our forecasts when the next quarterly GDP figures arrive,” he said.You use AI every day.
